context.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system evaluates card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud prior to approval and provides a case management workflow for fraud analysts. It operates on AWS within a strict PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance framework.

## Key Elements
* Payment Gateway / Acquirer Systems: External actor submitting payment authorizations.
* Fraud Analysts: Internal actors reviewing suspicious transactions.
* Regulatory / Compliance Auditors: External actors verifying 7-year audit logs.
* Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening System: Core software system handling scoring and case management.
* Identity Provider (IdP): External system managing authentication and RBAC.
* External Tokenization/Vault Service: External system handling card data.

## Relationships
* Payment Gateway to Screening System: Submits authorizations via gRPC/REST over TLS.
* Fraud Analysts to Screening System: Reviews payments via HTTPS.
* Auditors to Screening System: Accesses audit records via secure export/audit portal.
* Screening System to IdP: Authenticates users via OAuth2/OIDC over HTTPS.
* Screening System to Tokenization Service: Resolves payment tokens via gRPC/mTLS.

## Technology Stack
* AWS Cloud (eu-west-1): Selected as the target infrastructure provider within the 25,000 EUR monthly budget.
* AWS Cognito: Used as the Identity Provider to minimize operational overhead for a 3-engineer team.
* gRPC and REST over TLS: Protocol for high-throughput, low-latency payment ingestion.
* HTTPS: Protocol for secure analyst web interface access.
* mTLS: Protocol for secure integration with the tokenization service.

## Rationale
This architecture separates high-throughput synchronous scoring from asynchronous analyst reviews to easily meet the 50 ms P99 latency constraint at 3,000 TPS. Leveraging AWS-managed components satisfies PCI-DSS Level 1 security and 7-year auditability requirements while respecting the limits of a small engineering team and fixed budget.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system screens card-not-present payment authorizations in AWS for a mid-size payment processor. It provides real-time scoring, analyst case management, and tamper-evident auditing.

## Key Elements
* Payment Gateway / Acquirer Systems
* Fraud Analysts and Auditors
* AWS API Gateway (REST)
* Scoring Engine (Go microservice on AWS ECS Fargate)
* Case Management Backend (Node.js/Go service on ECS Fargate)
* Amazon DynamoDB and Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL
* Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose and Amazon S3 with Object Lock

## Relationships
* Payment Gateway to AWS API Gateway via HTTPS/JSON for authorization requests
* Scoring Engine to Amazon DynamoDB via AWS SDK for rule/model state
* Scoring Engine to Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose via HTTPS for audit logs
* Kinesis Data Firehose to Amazon S3 Object Lock for 7-year immutable retention
* Fraud Analysts to Case Management Backend via HTTPS for case reviews

## Technology Stack
* AWS ECS (Fargate) for minimal operational overhead with a 3-engineer team
* Go for the Scoring Engine to ensure sub-50ms P99 latency at 3,000 req/s
* Amazon DynamoDB for low-latency state and audit logs
* Amazon S3 with Object Lock for PCI-DSS Level 1 compliant tamper-evident storage

## Rationale
This architecture uses serverless and managed AWS components to meet strict PCI-DSS and audit requirements while staying within a 25,000 EUR monthly budget. It prioritizes low-latency technologies (Go, ECS Fargate, DynamoDB) to achieve sub-50ms P99 performance at scale.

AWS API Gateway.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system screens card-not-present payment authorizations in real-time and provides case management for fraud analysts. It ensures PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance, tamper-evident 7-year auditability, and sub-50ms P99 latency.

## Key Elements
- Payment Gateway / Acquirer Systems (External)
- Fraud Analysts (User)
- AWS API Gateway (REST) with native Request Validator, Authorizer, and HTTP Proxy Integration
- Scoring Engine (Go on AWS ECS Fargate)
- Case Management Backend (Node.js/Go on AWS ECS Fargate)
- Amazon DynamoDB and Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL
- Amazon S3 Object Lock & Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose

## Relationships
- Payment Gateway -> AWS API Gateway: Submits auth requests [HTTPS/JSON, mTLS]
- AWS API Gateway -> Scoring Engine: Routes requests for real-time scoring [Internal HTTP/REST over VPC Link]
- Scoring Engine -> Amazon DynamoDB: Queries rules and stores operational state [Internal AWS SDK]
- Case Management Backend -> Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL: Stores case data and analyst reviews [Internal TLS]
- System -> Amazon S3 Object Lock: Archives tamper-evident decision logs for 7 years [AWS SDK]

## Technology Stack
- AWS API Gateway (REST): Edge routing, JSON schema validation, and mTLS authorization for low latency
- Go & Node.js: High-performance backend services on AWS ECS Fargate
- Amazon DynamoDB & Aurora PostgreSQL: Low-latency NoSQL and relational data storage
- Amazon S3 with Object Lock: Tamper-evident 7-year audit retention
- AWS (eu-west-1): Cloud infrastructure complying with PCI-DSS Level 1

## Rationale
This architecture uses serverless and managed AWS services to meet the strict 50ms P99 latency constraint while staying within a 25,000 EUR monthly budget for a 3-engineer team. Native edge validation and VPC routing ensure high security and PCI-DSS compliance without adding infrastructure overhead.

Scoring Engine.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system evaluates card-not-present payment authorizations to approve, decline, or flag transactions for review while providing analyst case management. It ensures PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance, sub-50ms P99 latency at 3,000 TPS, and 7-year tamper-evident auditability within a fixed AWS budget.

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analysts, Regulatory / Compliance Auditors
- Payment Gateway / Acquirer Systems, Identity Provider (IdP), External Tokenization/Vault Service
- AWS API Gateway (REST)
- Scoring Engine (Go, AWS ECS Fargate)
- Case Management Backend (Node.js/Go, AWS ECS Fargate)
- HTTP Handler / Router Component
- Rule Evaluator Component (In-memory AST)
- Model Scoring Component (Embedded ONNX Runtime / compiled decision trees)
- Audit Dispatcher Component (Worker pools)
- Amazon DynamoDB, Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL
- Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose, Amazon S3 with Object Lock

## Relationships
- Payment Gateway / Acquirer Systems -> AWS API Gateway: Inbound authorization requests [HTTPS/REST]
- AWS API Gateway -> Scoring Engine: Routes requests for scoring [HTTP/REST over TCP with connection pooling]
- Scoring Engine -> Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL / Amazon DynamoDB: Reads compiled rule definitions and model state [AWS SDK / `pgx` pool over TLS]
- Scoring Engine -> Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose: Sends asynchronous audit logs [HTTPS]
- Scoring Engine -> Amazon S3 Object Lock: Stores tamper-evident immutable audit trails [AWS SDK over HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- Go (`net/http`): Selected for high-concurrency and low-latency execution in the Scoring Engine.
- ONNX Runtime / Compiled Decision Trees: Embedded in-memory model scoring to meet the <50ms P99 latency requirement.
- Amazon DynamoDB & Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL: Used for low-latency rule/model state retrieval and relational caching.
- Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose & Amazon S3 Object Lock: Implements WORM (Write Once, Read Many) storage to satisfy 7-year regulatory compliance.
- AWS ECS Fargate: Provides managed container orchestration within the 25,000 EUR monthly budget.

## Rationale
This architecture uses Go-based microservices with in-memory evaluation and connection pooling on AWS ECS Fargate to achieve sub-50ms latency at high throughput. Asynchronous audit dispatching and S3 Object Lock guarantee tamper-evident 7-year compliance without impacting real-time performance.

Case Management Backend.analysis:
## Overview
The Case Management Backend is a container within the Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system that enables fraud analysts to review suspicious transactions. It securely processes case workflows and maintains compliance while adhering to strict PCI-DSS Level 1 constraints.

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analysts: External users reviewing suspicious payments.
- Case API Handler (Node.js/Express): Manages incoming analyst HTTP requests.
- Case Workflow Engine (Go): Executes state transitions and business logic.
- Data Access Repository: Enforces data masking and queries the database.
- Audit Logger Component: Generates and exports tamper-evident compliance trails.
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL: Stores case data.
- Amazon S3 Object Lock: Stores immutable audit logs.

## Relationships
- Fraud Analysts -> Case API Handler: Manages cases [HTTPS/REST]
- Case API Handler -> Case Workflow Engine: Invokes business logic [Internal Function Call / gRPC]
- Case Workflow Engine -> Data Access Repository: Persists case state [In-memory / Go interfaces]
- Data Access Repository -> Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL: Reads/writes masked case data [SQL/TCP]
- Case Workflow Engine -> Audit Logger Component: Dispatches audit events [Internal Async / Channel]
- Audit Logger Component -> Amazon S3 Object Lock: Persists tamper-evident audit logs [AWS SDK / HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- Node.js/Express (Case API Handler): Selected for rapid UI-driven feature iteration by a small engineering team.
- Go (Case Workflow Engine, Data Access Repository, Audit Logger): Chosen for high performance, strong typing, and concurrency support.
- AWS ECS Fargate: Chosen to minimize operational overhead for a three-engineer team within a 25,000 EUR monthly budget.
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL: Relational storage enforcing strict PCI-DSS data masking.
- Amazon S3 Object Lock: Provides tamper-evident, write-once-read-many (WORM) storage for 7-year audit requirements.

## Rationale
This architecture balances rapid feature delivery for analysts with strict PCI-DSS and 7-year audit requirements using lightweight serverless containers. The clear separation of concerns ensures card data remains masked while satisfying all non-functional constraints within budget.

Amazon DynamoDB.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system evaluates card-not-present payment authorizations to detect fraud and provides case management workflows for analysts. It is deployed on AWS in region `eu-west-1` to meet strict compliance, low-latency, and budgetary constraints.

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analysts, Regulatory / Compliance Auditors
- Payment Gateway / Acquirer Systems, Identity Provider (IdP), External Tokenization/Vault Service
- AWS API Gateway (REST)
- Scoring Engine (Go, AWS ECS Fargate)
- Case Management Backend (Node.js/Go, AWS ECS Fargate)
- Amazon DynamoDB (`FraudRulesTable`, `CaseManagementTable`)
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL
- Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose
- Amazon S3 with Object Lock

## Relationships
- Scoring Engine -> `FraudRulesTable`: Reads and writes rule/model state via AWS SDK / HTTPS (TCP 443) using Consistent Read
- Case Management Backend -> `CaseManagementTable`: Reads and writes analyst workflow state via AWS SDK / HTTPS (TCP 443)
- Payment Gateway -> AWS API Gateway: Submits authorization requests via HTTPS (REST)

## Technology Stack
- AWS API Gateway: Manages and secures incoming HTTP REST traffic
- Go & Node.js on AWS ECS Fargate: Provides high-throughput, low-latency containerized compute within budget
- Amazon DynamoDB: Single-table design with composite primary keys (`RuleType`, `RuleID`) for sub-50ms rule retrieval
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL: Relational storage for transactional case management data

Amazon S3 Object Lock.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system screens card-not-present payment authorizations in real time and provides case management for fraud analysts. It ensures PCI-DSS compliance and immutable 7-year auditability on AWS within a fixed budget.

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analysts, Regulatory / Compliance Auditors
- Payment Gateway / Acquirer Systems, Identity Provider (IdP), External Tokenization/Vault Service
- AWS API Gateway (REST)
- Scoring Engine (Go, AWS ECS Fargate)
- Case Management Backend (Node.js/Go, AWS ECS Fargate)
- Amazon DynamoDB, Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL
- Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose
- Amazon S3 Object Lock: S3 Bucket with Object Lock (Compliance Mode), Bucket Lifecycle Policy Manager (AWS S3 Lifecycle), AWS KMS Encryption Key (AWS KMS)

## Relationships
- Payment Gateway -> AWS API Gateway: Submits authorization requests [HTTPS / JSON]
- Fraud Analysts -> AWS API Gateway: Manages suspicious payment cases [HTTPS / REST]
- AWS API Gateway -> Scoring Engine: Routes payment requests for evaluation [gRPC / Internal VPC]
- Scoring Engine -> Amazon DynamoDB: Fetches rules and caches fraud states [AWS SDK]
- Case Management Backend -> Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL: Stores analyst decisions and cases [PostgreSQL Wire Protocol]
- Scoring Engine -> Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose: Streams transaction decisions [AWS SDK]
- Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose -> S3 Bucket with Object Lock: Persists immutable audit logs [AWS S3 API / HTTPS]
- S3 Bucket with Object Lock -> AWS KMS: Encrypts and decrypts audit objects [AWS KMS API]
- Regulatory / Compliance Auditors -> S3 Bucket with Object Lock: Inspects audit logs [AWS Athena / S3 GET]

## Technology Stack
- AWS (eu-west-1): Target cloud infrastructure within budget
- Go and Node.js: High-performance backend services for low latency
- AWS ECS Fargate: Container orchestration minimizing operational overhead for 3 engineers
- Amazon DynamoDB and Aurora PostgreSQL: Scalable persistence layers
- AWS KMS (AES-256): Customer-managed keys ensuring PCI-DSS encryption
- Amazon S3 Object Lock (Compliance Mode): WORM storage enforcing 7-year immutable audit retention

## Rationale
This architecture uses managed AWS services to meet the strict sub-50ms latency and PCI-DSS requirements without exceeding the 25,000 EUR monthly budget. S3 Object Lock and KMS guarantee tamper-evident 7-year auditability while minimizing operational complexity for a three-engineer team.
